channel.title: doyouknow.app - English
channel.description: Surprising facts about UAE, Saudi Arabia, and the world.

item.title: How Buy Now, Pay Later Plans Actually Work
item.description: Tabby and Tamara make money from merchant fees, not shoppers, but missed instalments trigger late fees and can quietly affect your standing with the provider.

item.title: How Cashback Apps Actually Calculate What They Pay You
item.description: Cashback apps do not pay from their own pocket. They pass on a slice of the affiliate commission a merchant already pays, which is why rates fluctuate and payouts have rules.

item.title: How Credit Card Cashback and Miles Are Calculated
item.description: Card cashback and air miles are funded by the interchange fee merchants pay, not the bank's generosity, and redemption value often falls well short of the advertised earn rate.

item.title: How Dubai Shopping Festival's Raffle Prizes Actually Work
item.description: Dubai Duty Free's Millennium Millionaire and other DSF raffles sell a fixed number of tickets against a fixed prize pool. Here is how the odds and draws actually work.

item.title: How Duty-Free Pricing Actually Works at the Airport
item.description: Duty-free saves real money on alcohol, tobacco and perfume where tax removal is large, but on electronics and fashion the saving often shrinks once airport rent is priced back in.

item.title: How Exchange Rates Quietly Change What You Pay Shopping Online
item.description: The checkout prompt asking to pay in your home currency usually carries a worse exchange rate than your card network's conversion. Here is how that markup works.

item.title: How Extended Warranty Plans Actually Work
item.description: Extended warranties are priced using the same actuarial math as insurance, and that math favors the seller. Here is when a plan is genuinely worth buying and when it is not.

item.title: How Return and Refund Policies Actually Work in the UAE
item.description: In the UAE, a store letting you return an unwanted item is a courtesy, not a legal right, but a defective item triggers real protection under federal consumer law.

item.title: How Stores Decide That "70% Off" Number
item.description: A 70% off tag is a psychology tool, not a receipt. Here is how retailers set the reference price, and how to check whether a discount reflects real value.

item.title: How Supermarket Loyalty Cards Actually Save You Money
item.description: Loyalty cards from Carrefour, Lulu, and others save money on some baskets and none on others. The difference comes down to points math and the non-member price.

item.title: How to Read a Price-Per-Unit Label While Grocery Shopping
item.description: The unit price on a shelf label, not the pack price, is the only number that compares products fairly. Here is how to read it and where bulk packs quietly stop being a deal.

item.title: How to Spot a Fake "Was / Now" Discount
item.description: A well-documented retail tactic raises the "was" price right before a sale starts. Here is how to catch it and check before trusting the tag.

item.title: How to Tell a Fake Online Store From a Real One
item.description: Fake online stores share recognisable patterns, a domain registered weeks ago, no real contact address, payment-only-by-transfer, and prices far below every competitor's.

item.title: Why the Same Product Shows a Different Price on Different Apps
item.description: The same product can show two different prices to two different shoppers at the same moment. Here is what actually drives that gap, and how to consistently see the lower one.

item.title: Why Electronics Get Cheaper Right Before a New Model Launches
item.description: Flagship phones and laptops follow a predictable discount cycle: retailers quietly cut prices on outgoing stock before a new generation lands. Here is the rhythm.

item.title: Why Flash Sales Make You Buy Faster Than You Planned
item.description: Countdown timers and "only 3 left" labels are documented psychological tactics that shorten decision time. A deliberate pause is the simplest defense against them.

item.title: Why Gold Prices Change Every Day, and When to Buy
item.description: Gulf gold rates move daily because they track the international spot price through the USD/AED peg, then add karat purity and making charges. Here is how that chain works.

item.title: Why Ramadan Sales Happen, and What Actually Gets Discounted
item.description: Ramadan sales in the UAE, Saudi Arabia, and Egypt follow a predictable retail calendar, groceries and abayas discount early, electronics wait for the Eid rush.

item.title: Why the Same Perfume Costs Different Prices in Different Shops
item.description: The same perfume can cost noticeably different amounts across a mall, duty-free, and an online store, driven by concentration, channel economics, and brand markup, not randomness.

item.title: Why White Friday Is Called White Friday, Not Black Friday
item.description: White Friday is a UAE retail invention, not a rebrand of Black Friday. Here is where the name actually came from, when it lands, and what discounts by category really look like.
